images.title: Half of which roti
images.purpose: Show that 1/2 of a small roti and 1/2 of a big roti are different amounts, and that 1/2 against 1/4 can be compared only when the two rotis are the same size.
images.composition: Left panel: a small roti of 10 pieces and a big roti of 16 pieces, half of each shaded. Right panel: two rotis of the same size with 12 pieces each, one with a half and one with a quarter shaded.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, two panels side by side separated by one thin construction grey #6B7280 vertical line at x 770 from y 140 to y 700. Every roti is a circle cut from its centre into equal pieces (wedges) by thin dark #2B2B2B cut lines (3 px), the first cut line pointing straight up (12 o'clock) and the pieces counted clockwise from it. Unshaded pieces are white. The circle radii are chosen so that every one of the 50 pieces in the frame has the same area (about 4,500 square px). Panel headings, dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px), centred at y 90: Different sizes at x 380 over the left panel and Same size at x 1105 over the right panel. LEFT PANEL, two rotis with centres at y 340. (1) Small roti: centre x 210, radius 120, cut into exactly 10 equal pieces of 36 degrees; the first 5 pieces (the right half) shaded teal #0072B2, the other 5 white. (2) Big roti: centre x 550, radius 152, cut into exactly 16 equal pieces of 22.5 degrees; the first 8 pieces (the right half) shaded amber #E69F00, the other 8 white. Under the small roti, centred at x 210, the name Small roti at y 550 (36 px) and the line 1/2 = 5 pieces at y 615 (38 px bold). Under the big roti, centred at x 550, the name Big roti at y 550 (36 px) and the line 1/2 = 8 pieces at y 615 (38 px bold). RIGHT PANEL, two rotis of the same size, both with centres at y 340 and radius 131. (3) Left roti: centre x 950, cut into exactly 12 equal pieces of 30 degrees; the first 6 pieces (the right half) shaded teal #0072B2, the other 6 white. (4) Right roti: centre x 1260, also cut into exactly 12 equal pieces of 30 degrees; the first 3 pieces (the top right quarter) shaded amber #E69F00, the other 9 white. Under them, centred at y 615 (38 px bold): 1/2 = 6 pieces under the left roti and 1/4 = 3 pieces under the right roti. In all there are 4 rotis and 10 + 16 + 12 + 12 = 50 pieces. No other numbers, no arrows. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Half of a small whole and half of a big whole are different amounts, so two fractions can be compared only when their wholes are the same size.
images.description: Four rotis cut into equal pieces: a small roti of 10 pieces and a big roti of 16 pieces with half of each shaded, then two rotis of the same size, each in 12 pieces, with 1/2 and 1/4 shaded.
images.context: Concept image for Same Whole, Fair Comparison. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (rotis of different sizes with half marked, then rotis of the same size with half and a quarter) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example: 10, 16 and 12 pieces.
images.teaching_notes: Count the shaded pieces aloud: 5 and 8 are both called 1/2, but they are not the same amount. The slip to watch: thinking that 1/2 is always the same amount, whatever the whole.

image_decisions.why: The small roti, the big roti and the two same-size rotis show at a glance why a fraction is a part of its own whole and why the wholes must match to compare.
